story: University of Alaska regents weigh AI Engaged, a systemwide AI statement whose first draft two UAA professors say Anthropic's Claude wrote, while faculty on the advisory committee push back

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that the University of Alaska Board of Regents would vote on November 5th on its AI statement.
claims.verbatim: Now, the University of Alaska Board of Regents will vote on Nov. 5 to enshrine Claude's pro-artificial intelligence vision:
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: Page reads Published November 4, 2026 although the URL path is 2026/11/03. Primary only for what the authors wrote. Vote OUTCOME unconfirmed; see killed.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter quote the statement as saying the Board of Regents declares its intent for the University of Alaska to embrace artificial intelligence as a strategic enabler of student success, institutional effectiveness, and Alaska's global leadership in arctic and climate science.
claims.verbatim: The Board of Regents declares its intent for the University of Alaska to embrace artificial intelligence as a strategic enabler of student success, institutional effectiveness, and Alaska's global leadership in arctic and climate science.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: The op-ed's quotation of the statement; the statement itself was unreachable on alaska.edu (HTTP 503). Treat as quoted by Hartley and Potter.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that the board commissioned a strategic document called AI Engaged in June 2026.
claims.verbatim: In June 2026, the board commissioned a strategic document called AI Engaged,
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: Conflicts with the UA release (C31, May). Attribute June to Hartley and Potter only, or use UA's May wording.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft of AI Engaged.
claims.verbatim: Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft, a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: ALLEGATION, always attributed. The rebuttal (C13, C16) does not deny AI drafting. No UA primary document confirming Claude's role was reachable.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that the use of Claude was concealed for months until October 9th.
claims.verbatim: Anthropic's Claude generated the initial draft, a fact concealed for months until Oct. 9.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: DISPUTED by C13. Give both sides.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that the disclosure came too late and remains incomplete.
claims.verbatim: Disclosure came too late and remains incomplete.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that studies have documented a pro-AI bias in outputs from Claude and other large language models.
claims.verbatim: Studies have documented a pro-AI bias in outputs from Claude and other large language models.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: Studies not checked. Use only as the authors' assertion.

claims.claim: Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter are associate professors at the University of Alaska Anchorage.
claims.verbatim: Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter serve as associate professors at the University of Alaska Anchorage.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that the regents should abandon the document and establish safeguards against undue influence from Big Tech.
claims.verbatim: The UA Board of Regents should abandon the document and go back to the drawing board to establish best practices and safeguards against undue influence from Big Tech and its hype machine.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that UA board members and administrative executives are not required to disclose financial holdings in education or technology companies.
claims.verbatim: Currently, board members and administrative executives in the University of Alaska are not required to disclose financial holdings in education or technology companies.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)
claims.notes: Not independently checked against UA policy; keep attributed.

claims.claim: Hartley and Potter wrote that more members of the UA community should have been directly involved in drafting UA's AI plan.
claims.verbatim: More members of the UA community should have been directly involved in drafting UA's AI plan.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Gregory Hartley and Joel Potter)

claims.claim: A rebuttal op-ed by five UA faculty members wrote that anyone who met with administrators and board members knew how the original draft was constructed.
claims.verbatim: Anyone who met with administrators and board members knew how the original draft was constructed.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: Five-author count from the byline (Jennifer Carroll, Jackie Cason, James Ryan, Andrew Harnish, Erin Trochim).

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that AI use in drafting the statement was not concealed.
claims.verbatim: In this case, AI use was not "concealed."
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that the regents were already pro-AI before the draft.
claims.verbatim: We can assure you, and we are sure the board would also assure you, that they were already pro-AI.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that they would prefer the statement take a more neutral stance toward AI.
claims.verbatim: One of these disagreements is that we would prefer the statement take a more neutral stance toward AI.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: The defenders of the process also disagree with the pro-AI tilt.

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that eventually adding a small AI attribution was a good move.
claims.verbatim: Eventually adding a small AI attribution was a good move, given the various perspectives and norms,
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: Implies the attribution was added later.

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that the work behind the statement began with a September 2025 AI symposium funded by the Faculty Alliance Faculty Initiative Fund.
claims.verbatim: The labor that eventually resulted in the Board of Regents' statement of intent on AI began with a September 2025 AI symposium funded by the Faculty Alliance Faculty Initiative Fund.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: Year stays: a different calendar year.

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that the symposium produced the UA AI Coordinating Council.
claims.verbatim: Among the outcomes of that faculty-organized and -led symposium was the UA AI Coordinating Council.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)

claims.claim: James Ryan, one of the rebuttal authors, chairs the UA Statewide Advisory Committee and teaches writing at the University of Alaska Southeast.
claims.verbatim: James Ryan is chair of the UA Statewide Advisory Committee and an assistant professor of writing
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)
claims.notes: Other roles per bio lines: Carroll former Faculty Alliance chair, UAF Alaska Native studies; Trochim UAF Institute of Northern Engineering; Cason former Faculty Alliance chair, UAA writing; Harnish UAA writing.

claims.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that UAF faculty member Jennifer Carroll and Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier gave a joint presentation to the regents in May.
claims.verbatim: from that came a joint presentation to the Board of Regents by UAF faculty member Jennifer Carroll and Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier in May.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (opinion, Carroll, Cason, Ryan, Harnish and Trochim)

claims.claim: KTOO reported that the draft AI policy would require all three University of Alaska campuses to have an AI plan for students, faculty and staff.
claims.verbatim: If approved, it would require all three campuses to have an AI plan in place for students, faculty and staff.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO (Jamie Diep)
claims.notes: Background. Also on the Alaska Public Media republication of September 18th.

claims.claim: KTOO reported in September that university leadership planned to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.verbatim: University leadership plans to submit a finalized draft for approval at the November regents meeting.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO (Jamie Diep)

claims.claim: KTOO cited a 2025 Inside Higher Ed survey finding that about 85 percent of college students use generative AI in their coursework.
claims.verbatim: It finds that about 85% of college students use generative AI in their coursework.
claims.source_outlet: KTOO via Alaska Public Media (Jamie Diep)
claims.notes: National survey, not an Alaska figure.

claims.claim: ADN reported that of 150 UAA students cited for academic misconduct, 119 used AI, according to a Dean of Students Office report released in August.
claims.verbatim: Of the 150 students cited for academic misconduct, 119 used AI,
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Tim Rockey)

claims.claim: ADN reported that the AI cases accounted for 1.1 percent of the more than 10,500 students who attended UAA last semester.
claims.verbatim: accounting for 1.1% of the more than 10,500 students who attended UAA last semester.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Tim Rockey)

claims.claim: ADN reported that the UAA report showed a 73 percent increase in AI use for plagiarism last year and a 56 percent increase in academic misconduct overall.
claims.verbatim: The report shows a 73% increase in AI use for plagiarism last year and a 56% increase in academic misconduct overall.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Tim Rockey)

claims.claim: The UA system does not have a single policy governing AI use across more than a dozen campuses, ADN reported.
claims.verbatim: The UA system does not have a single policy governing AI use across more than a dozen individual campuses.
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Tim Rockey)
claims.notes: True as of October 4th; outcome of the vote unknown.

claims.claim: ADN reported that the draft guiding principles call for appropriate AI in every discipline and say humans must remain in the loop.
claims.verbatim: which calls for "appropriate AI in every discipline" and emphasizes that humans must remain "in the loop."
claims.source_outlet: Anchorage Daily News (Tim Rockey)

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said its Board of Regents would meet in Fairbanks on the UAF campus from November 4th to 6th and consider new guidelines for AI use.
claims.verbatim: The University of Alaska (UA) Board of Regents will meet in Fairbanks, November 4-6, on the University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) campus to consider the proposed FY28 budget, a new tuition structure, update policies and consider new guidelines for AI use.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier would share the latest version of AI Engaged at the November meeting.
claims.verbatim: Chief Information Technology Officer Ben Shier will share the latest version of UA's "AI Engaged" effort.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said that in May the Board directed UA leadership to develop a cohesive strategy on artificial intelligence.
claims.verbatim: In May, the Board directed UA leadership to develop a cohesive strategy around the university's approach to artificial intelligence from a philosophical, pedagogical and operational lens.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said the AI statement establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations.
claims.verbatim: The statement establishes six guiding principles, four investment priorities and five system-wide expectations for each university's AI work,
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said the statement preserves UAA, UAF and UAS responsibility for curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment.
claims.verbatim: setting system-level direction while preserving UAA, UAF and UAS responsibility for curriculum, academic integrity and faculty instructional judgment.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska said the final AI document incorporates feedback from students, faculty and staff across the system.
claims.verbatim: The final document incorporates feedback from students, faculty and staff across the system.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire

claims.claim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents is an 11-member volunteer board.
claims.verbatim: The University of Alaska Board of Regents is an 11-member volunteer board.
claims.source_outlet: University of Alaska, news release via EIN Presswire
claims.notes: Same release, enrollment just over 20,000 students.

claims.claim: North of 60 Mining News reported that the UAF-led critical minerals engine was one of 12 teams chosen from 294 initial applications.
claims.verbatim: the select group of 12 teams chosen from a national competition that began with 294 initial applications
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley)

claims.claim: North of 60 Mining News reported that the NSF award provides $15 million over the first two years with the potential for another $145 million over the next decade.
claims.verbatim: The award provides $15 million over the first two years
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley)

claims.claim: North of 60 Mining News reported that the engine intends to advance AI-enabled technologies to accelerate mineral exploration.
claims.verbatim: The project also intends to advance AI-enabled technologies that can accelerate mineral exploration, characterization, and deposit delineation.
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley)

claims.claim: North of 60 Mining News reported that Alaska hosts occurrences of 56 of the 60 minerals deemed critical to the United States.
claims.verbatim: sits in the heart of a state that hosts occurrences of 56 of the 60 minerals deemed critical to America's economic and national security.
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley)

claims.claim: North of 60 Mining News reported that the engine's network includes more than 50 partners, among them Teck Resources, operator of Red Dog.
claims.verbatim: Today, our network includes more than 50 partners,
claims.source_outlet: North of 60 Mining News (Shane Lasley)

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that the Regulatory Commission of Alaska approved an exchange agreement among Enstar, Matanuska Electric Association and Hilcorp in late October.
claims.verbatim: The Regulatory Commission of Alaska approved an exchange agreement in late October.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Ava White)

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that the agreement allows Enstar to buy about 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
claims.verbatim: allows Enstar to buy about 1.2 billion cubic feet of natural gas.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Ava White)

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that the deal boosts Enstar's year-end storage projection to about 5 billion cubic feet against a goal of 6 to 7 billion.
claims.verbatim: This agreement boosts projections to about 5 billion cubic feet, he said.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Ava White)

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that Enstar must deliver the equivalent gas back to MEA by March 2028.
claims.verbatim: Enstar has to deliver the equivalent amount of natural gas back to MEA by March 2028.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Ava White)

claims.claim: Alaska Public Media reported that MEA predicts the agreement will save its customers about $2 million between 2027 and 2029.
claims.verbatim: predicts the agreement will save customers about $2 million between 2027 and 2029.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Public Media (Ava White)

stories_surviving: University of Alaska regents weigh AI Engaged, the AI statement two UAA professors say Claude first drafted
UAF Critical Minerals Accelerator Engine wins NSF award with industry backing and AI-enabled exploration plans
RCA approves Enstar, MEA and Hilcorp gas exchange of about 1.2 Bcf for Southcentral winter

killed.claim: The Board of Regents adopted, rejected or delayed the AI statement at its November 5th meeting.
killed.why: Unverified. alaska.edu/bor, alaska.edu/news/system and alaska.edu/ai/policies all returned HTTP 503 today; the Alaska Public Media and ADN education indexes list no November item on the vote; the UA release of November 3rd reports only a planned presentation. Assert no outcome.

killed.claim: The rebuttal authors wrote that AI was used to create the draft from original documents supplied by stakeholders.
killed.why: Misstated by a summarizer. The verbatim sentence describes what others think is acceptable, not the process.

killed.claim: The UAF engine will use AI to merge drill logs and geophysics.
killed.why: Not on the page as phrased; replaced by C38.

killed.claim: North of 60 Mining News published the engine story on October 30th.
Hartley and Potter's financial disclosure ask, as a verbatim quote.
killed.why: Recommendation sentence not captured verbatim; C10 only.

killed.claim: The board commissioned AI Engaged in June 2026, stated as fact.
killed.why: Conflicts with the UA release (May). Kept only as attributed C03.

killed.claim: Alaska Current Sullivan donations, Fairbanks town hall, Senate coalition leadership.
